# orchestration_cluster_cluster_variable (Data Source)

Looks up a variable inside a Camunda cluster by name, either global or scoped to a single tenant. See the Camunda documentation on [cluster variables](https://docs.camunda.io/docs/components/admin/cluster-variables/). The value is stored in the Terraform state and is **not** marked sensitive: do not store secrets in cluster variables.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A global cluster variable.
data "orchestration_cluster_cluster_variable" "global" {
  name = "default-retries"
}

# A tenant-scoped cluster variable: set tenant_id.
data "orchestration_cluster_cluster_variable" "tenant" {
  name      = "greeting"
  tenant_id = "my-tenant"
}

# The value is a JSON document.
output "default_retries" {
  value = jsondecode(data.orchestration_cluster_cluster_variable.global.value)
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the cluster variable to look up.

### Optional

- `tenant_id` (String) The ID of the tenant the variable is scoped to. Omit it to look up a global variable.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The identity of the variable: `GLOBAL/<name>` for a global variable or `TENANT/<tenant_id>/<name>` for a tenant-scoped one.
- `kind` (String) The kind of the variable: `JSON` or `SECRET_REFERENCE`. The value of a `SECRET_REFERENCE` variable holds `camunda.secrets.<name>` references, not the secrets themselves.
- `metadata` (Map of String) Key-value metadata attached to the variable, or null if it has none. Numeric metadata values are reported as their string representation.
- `scope` (String) The scope of the variable: `GLOBAL` or `TENANT`.
- `value` (String) The value of the variable as a JSON document, the same way the `orchestration_cluster_cluster_variable` resource reports it. Use `jsondecode()` to read it.
